tasks.title: Document a mature workbench extraction boundary
tasks.objective: Trace a mature workbench's agent launch planning, PTY lifecycle, native hook status normalization, and Claude Agent Teams tmux special case into an evidence-backed extraction note.
tasks.outcome: The implementation has a source-linked map of what to borrow, simplify, and deliberately omit.
acceptance: The note covers Codex, Claude, Hermes, and Pi launch and status paths.
The note distinguishes normal node-pty hosting from the Claude Agent Teams tmux shim.
Every material claim links to a repository-relative a mature workbench source path and line reference.

verification.proves: The extraction decisions are grounded in the inspected a mature workbench implementation.

tasks.title: Build reusable tmux agent runtime
tasks.objective: Implement the public Provider core, local/SSH ExecutionHost boundary, tmux process boundary, output follower, normalized status/activity model, hook ingress, and four built-in agent adapters.
tasks.outcome: Node consumers can configure, launch, observe, control, and stop supported agents on local or SSH tmux hosts through one typed API.
acceptance: All tmux commands use argument arrays and package-owned session names.
LocalHost and SshHost satisfy the same ExecutionHost contract and have deterministic transport tests.
Codex, Claude, Hermes, and Pi produce correct deterministic launch plans.
Status events identify native-hook versus fallback provenance.
Observable prompt, assistant, tool, permission, lifecycle, and raw-output activity can be projected without claiming private chain-of-thought.
A real tmux integration test proves lifecycle, output, input, exit, and cleanup.

verification.proves: Core unit and real-tmux integration behavior passes.
The reusable runtime is exposed through one public package boundary.

tasks.title: Build terminal-first conversational workbench
tasks.objective: Implement a thin Electron/React consumer with terminal-first startup, raw-terminal and conversation projections, Warp-style rich input, host/agent configuration and controls, rooted local/remote file editing, tabs, and resizable split panes.
tasks.outcome: A developer can operate one tmux session as either a terminal or a readable conversation/activity stream while editing the same workspace.
acceptance: The renderer never imports Node or tmux primitives directly.
Workspace file reads and writes are root-confined in main-process IPC.
Agent configuration and session controls consume the core package public API.
Users can select a configured local or SSH host for workspace and session operations.
The main workbench supports resizable navigator, editor, and agent-console regions with tabs.
Rich input supports multi-line prompts and contextual file references.
Terminal and conversation modes are two projections of the same session and expose event provenance.

verification.proves: The core package and desktop main, preload, and renderer production bundles compile.
The demonstrator exposes the required workbench capabilities.

tasks.title: Build workspace board and worktree automation
tasks.objective: Add an workbench-style workspace board plus explicit local/SSH Git worktree creation that automatically registers the resulting host-scoped workspace and can launch an agent there.
tasks.outcome: Repositories, worktrees, and their active agent sessions are navigable as both a sidebar hierarchy and a status board.
acceptance: The board groups workspace cards by normalized agent state and shows branch/path/session evidence.
Worktree creation uses Git argument arrays and happens only after explicit confirmation.
Remote worktree creation and workspace file operations execute through the selected SshHost without persisting private key material.
A successful worktree is registered as a workspace; a failed Git command leaves no phantom workspace.
Workspace selection restores its tabs/splits and defaults to the terminal surface.

verification.proves: Git worktree mutation and workspace registration have one audited main-process owner.
The desktop exposes the required workspace-as-board projection.

tasks.title: Verify and hand off the demonstrator
tasks.objective: Run the repository proof suite, inspect the rendered desktop surface, document setup and usage, and record residual limits.
tasks.outcome: The repository is reproducibly buildable and the user has a concise architectural and operational handoff.
acceptance: Install, typecheck, test, and build complete successfully.
README documents prerequisites, architecture, Provider/ExecutionHost API usage, desktop startup, SSH setup, and worktree flow.
Visual inspection confirms clear state hierarchy, usable terminal/chat modes, splits, board, empty/error states, and no overflow at the target window size.
Residual limits are explicit rather than presented as completed behavior.

verification.proves: All automated repository checks pass through one public command.
Desktop behavior and visual quality were manually inspected.
